level: In-depth engineering course · no official exam
name: TypeScript in Depth
audience: Developers who use TypeScript daily and want to master the type system, the JavaScript runtime beneath it and modern tooling for full-stack apps.
format: This site's course with a 40-question practice test of does-it-type-check, predict-the-output, type design and debugging questions.
scenarios: Migrating a codebase to strict mode
Debugging an async race in Node
Publishing a library with correct types
verifyNotes: This is the site's own in-depth engineering course, not a vendor certification: there are no exam facts to confirm, so spend Research on finding the best official/primary sources per topic (URLs that will be cited as sources) and on what is current as of November 2026. Goal: a senior engineer or architect who builds products alone or in a team of 2-3 can apply every idea confidently in real work, a design review or a senior interview. Lessons go deep: intuition first, then the precise mechanism, then a fully worked example with real numbers or code, then where it matters in production, then a common misconception. Write math in LaTeX between double dollars only: $$...$$; NEVER single-dollar math (single $ renders literally; in SQL or shell code use code fences). In JSON strings escape backslashes. Markdown tables: never put a raw | inside a cell (escape it as \\| or use \\lvert in math). Every lesson has a hands-on lab: a small exercise with the expected output. State any randomness seed. Question mix: ~35% does-this-type-check or what-type-is-inferred, ~25% predict the runtime output (event loop, promises, coercion, closures), ~40% design and debugging judgment. Code in fenced ```ts blocks. Verifiers MUST type-check and run every code example, lab and code question with `sh {{root}}/.pipeline/ts/check.sh <file.ts>` (TypeScript 7.0 native compiler with --strict, then Node 24 with type stripping) and fix keys that disagree; quote the exact compiler error code (e.g. TS2322) only when verified. Node type stripping does not support enums, namespaces with values or parameter properties (erasableSyntaxOnly): say so where relevant. Target TypeScript 7.x (the Go-based native compiler; note behaviour or option changes vs 5.x/6.x, such as removed options and new defaults, only if the release notes confirm them), ES2025 and Node 24 LTS. React examples follow React 19 and may be verified by type reasoning against react.dev. Sources: typescriptlang.org (handbook, tsconfig reference, release notes), devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript, github.com/microsoft/typescript-go, developer.mozilla.org, tc39.es, nodejs.org docs, react.dev, zod.dev and vitest.dev; no blogs or Medium.

domains.name: The type system foundations
skills: Structural typing, assignability, excess property checks and type widening
Inference, contextual typing, literal types, as const and satisfies
Unions and narrowing: typeof, in, instanceof, equality, type predicates and assertion functions
Discriminated unions and exhaustiveness checking with never
any vs unknown vs never, type assertions, and the soundness holes to know

domains.name: Advanced types
skills: Generics: constraints, defaults, inference from arguments, const type parameters
Conditional types, infer and distributive behaviour
Mapped types, key remapping with as, and template literal types
The built-in utility types and how they are implemented (Partial, Pick, Omit, Record, ReturnType, Awaited)
Variance, function parameter bivariance, overloads vs generics, and keeping types fast to check

domains.name: The JavaScript runtime beneath TypeScript
skills: The event loop: call stack, microtasks vs macrotasks, ordering of promises, timers and await
Promises and async/await: error propagation, unhandled rejections, Promise.all/allSettled/any/race, AbortController
this, closures, scope and hoisting; arrow functions vs methods
Equality, coercion, numbers (IEEE 754, BigInt) and common runtime surprises
Modules: ESM vs CommonJS, import/export semantics, top-level await, dynamic import

domains.name: Designing with types
skills: Modelling domains: making illegal states unrepresentable, branded and opaque types
Errors as values (Result types) vs exceptions; typing unknown errors in catch
Runtime validation at boundaries with Zod: schemas, z.infer, parsing vs validating
Type-safe APIs end to end: shared types, inference across client and server, OpenAPI generation
Declaration files, module augmentation, and typing third-party JavaScript

domains.name: Tooling, configuration and the TypeScript 7 compiler
skills: tsconfig essentials: strict family, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, target and lib
Module settings: module and moduleResolution (nodenext vs bundler), verbatimModuleSyntax, isolatedModules
Running TypeScript: tsc vs bundlers vs Node type stripping (erasableSyntaxOnly); the native TypeScript 7 compiler and its speed
Monorepos and project references; build performance and incremental builds
Publishing libraries: package.json exports and types conditions, dual ESM/CJS, declaration output

domains.name: TypeScript for full-stack apps
skills: Node.js with TypeScript: fetch, streams, events, worker threads and graceful shutdown
Typing HTTP handlers and middleware (Hono or Express style), request validation and typed responses
React 19 with TypeScript: props, children, events, refs, hooks and generic components
Testing TypeScript with Vitest: typed mocks, type tests with expectTypeOf
Linting and code quality: typescript-eslint rules that catch real bugs, strictness migration strategy
